questions.text: I routinely absorb extra costs in group situations so others pay less.
When someone's suffering is vivid to me, I feel a strong wish to ease it.
I carry the emotional tone of a dream well into my waking day.
I feel energized when a group reaches a genuine consensus.
I know a project is done when it feels complete, not when it meets predefined criteria.
My emotions feel like background music — always present, but never drowning out the rest of my experience.
I feel uncomfortable when I leave things half-finished at the end of the day.
I find it natural to tell others what I expect from them.
I keep a journal or log to reflect on my progress and hold myself accountable.
I notice that other people sometimes need to tell me a situation was intense because I didn't register it that way.
I work in intense bursts of energy rather than at a steady, measured pace.
Watching a person suffer usually stirs no wish in me to ease their suffering.
I run errands as they occur to me, sometimes doubling back, and that's fine by me.
I experience the stress of a tight schedule as a practical reality rather than a source of internal turmoil.
I don't turn away from suffering because it is complex or uncomfortable.
I can tell when a conversation's real audience is not the person being spoken to but someone who is overhearing.
I believe the measure of my day is how much I gave, not how much I gained.
When someone asks for my support in a hard time, I usually feel little wish to give it.
I am recognized for my ability to weave diverse viewpoints into a cohesive group effort.
I experience the ending of a meaningful chapter — a project, a season, a relationship — as a kind of small death.
I finalize plans early to give myself and others time to prepare.
I often catch the quick glance two people exchange when something significant is said.
I tend to accept invitations at face value without wondering if there is a subtext.
I prefer that big bets be discussed thoroughly with the group before anyone commits.
When something embarrassing happens, I can feel the heat in my face and neck for minutes afterward.
I often speak with an air of finality that signals the discussion is over.
I do not usually detect when a social environment has an unspoken expectation about reciprocity.
I pick up on the difference between someone who is quiet by nature and someone who has been silenced by the group.
I routinely advocate for my own interests in negotiations and discussions.
I tend to work extra hours not for my own advancement, but to lighten the load for my team.
I feel at home being the primary representative of a group to the outside world.
Reflecting on someone's difficulties often makes me wish I could ease them.
I do not naturally sense when a group has collectively moved on from a topic that one person still wants to discuss.
I find that building a strong personal financial cushion gives me more confidence than anything else.
I tend to view my personal bucket list as a binding contract with myself.
Others' need for help seldom gives me a reason to want to act.
